title: What is Brahman? (8.1–8.7)
hook: Arjuna fires off seven questions in a row, and the last one is about the moment of death

segments.voice: Yesterday: maya and the veil, the power that hides Krishna in plain sight. Your line was behind the veil. Chapter seven ended with a handful of big words. Today, Arjuna asks what they mean. Day one hundred eighty-six.
screen: `MAYA AND THE VEIL — BEHIND THE VEIL.`

segments.voice: A teacher uses five unfamiliar words in one sentence. Everyone else nods. One student finally raises a hand. That's Arjuna at the start of chapter eight. Krishna has just dropped a string of big terms. Brahman. The self. Action. And Arjuna doesn't nod. He asks, one after another: What is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? And then the question underneath all the others: at the time of death, how are you known?
screen: `FIVE UNFAMILIAR WORDS.` → `ARJUNA RAISES HIS HAND.` → `SEVEN QUESTIONS.`

segments.voice: Krishna answers them fast, one line each. Brahman, verse three, is the imperishable, the highest. The word akshara, imperishable, also means a syllable, a letter, something that can't be broken down further. The self, adhyatma, is one's own essential nature. Action, karma, is the creative outpouring that brings beings into existence. Then the perishable world of things, the cosmic person behind the gods, and, the Lord of sacrifice: Krishna himself, here, in this body. That's the dictionary. But then comes the part people remember. Verse five: whoever, at the time of the end, leaves the body remembering me alone, comes to my being. There's no doubt about it. And verse six widens it: whatever state a person remembers at the end, as they leave the body, to that state they go, because they've always been shaped by it. So the moment of death isn't a pop quiz. It's the sum of what you've been practicing all along. Which is why verse seven, the closing line of this section, is so practical. Therefore, at all times, remember me, and fight. Remember, and fight. Not remember instead of living; remember while living. Arjuna is still standing between two armies. Krishna doesn't tell him to go meditate in a cave until he dies. He says: keep me in mind, and do what's in front of you. That's the word today, what is Brahman? The imperishable. And the practical answer: remember, in the middle of everything.
screen: `SEVEN QUESTIONS.` · `BRAHMAN: THE IMPERISHABLE.` · `WHAT YOU REMEMBER AT THE END.` · `AT ALL TIMES, REMEMBER, AND FIGHT.` · then, large: `REMEMBER, WHILE LIVING.`

segments.voice: Verse six says we become what we're shaped by. So sit, and look at what you've been remembering lately. What comes to mind most often, when your mind is free? A worry, a person, a screen? Don't judge it. Then choose one thing you'd like to be shaped by: a name of God if you pray, a person you love, a line from this path. Return to it on every breath. The bell holds the time.
What is Brahman? Arjuna's first question. Krishna's answer: the imperishable, the highest. And then: remember me at all times.
Your line: remember me. Three times today, in the middle of something, bring to mind the one thing you chose, and keep going. Day one hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Some Hindus practice smarana, the constant remembering of God, by repeating a divine name through the day, and some families chant God's name at the bedside of someone who is dying, in the spirit of Gita 8.5–8.7.

fork.reveal: remember, and fight. keep him in mind while doing what's in front of you.

original.note: Sanskrit: akshara, imperishable; also a syllable or letter. Krishna's first definition of Brahman (8.3).

trapdoor: what you thought: Brahman is a caste.
what it means: Brahman is the imperishable, the highest reality; and the way to it is to remember, at all times.

what a scholar hears: Brahman (neuter, the absolute) is a different word from Brahma (the creator god) and brahmana (priest); 8.3 defines it as akshara, and 8.6 grounds the 'last thought' in a lifetime's bhava.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 8.5–8.7 (remember me at the end, and at all times)
